sections.h2: What is the quickest way to sell a house in Jupiter, FL?
sections.html:
The quickest route is usually a cash or as-is sale with clear title, because it removes lender underwriting and most repair negotiation. A listing with an agent can still close well, particularly for a move-in-ready home, but it depends on buyer financing, appraisal and inspection timing.

Jupiter is a town, not a city, in Palm Beach County, so recording and tax steps run through the county clerk, property appraiser and tax collector rather than a municipal office. Whichever way you sell, the deed must be written, signed before two subscribing witnesses and recorded.

  • List with an agent: broad exposure, more conditions, longer timeline.
  • Cash or as-is buyer: fewer conditions, you skip repairs and showings.
  • Sale to a family member: still treated as a conveyance for consideration.

sections.h2: What should sellers know about the town of Jupiter?
sections.html:
Jupiter's roots run along the Loxahatchee River and the Atlantic. The town's redevelopment history page says archaeological evidence shows human inhabitants as early as 500 BC, and that the Tequesta and Hobe peoples settled the shoreline. In the mid-1800s the federal government built the Jupiter Lighthouse, which helped establish the settlement that became the town. The Inlet Village area later served as a fishing village and a shipping port, with the Celestial Railroad running between Jupiter and Juno Beach.

Today the town is a high-income, owner-occupied community by Census measures. The July 2025 population estimate is 62,350, up 2.1 percent from the 2020 base, across 21.63 square miles of land. About 24.4 percent of residents are 65 or older, and 78.5 percent of homes are owner-occupied. The median owner-occupied home value for 2020 to 2024 is $608,600, and median gross rent is $2,381.

Household income is high as well. Median household income is $110,240, and 53.5 percent of adults 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree or higher.

sections.h2: How does Jupiter's older, owner-occupied population affect a sale?
sections.html:
Because roughly a quarter of residents are 65 or older and nearly four in five homes are owner-occupied, many Jupiter sales involve long-time owners, downsizing and estates. That makes the senior and probate rules in Florida worth knowing before you list.

  • Seniors: a county or city ordinance may allow an additional homestead exemption of up to $50,000 for owners 65 or older within an income limit, per the Department of Revenue. Ask the Palm Beach County Property Appraiser whether it applies to you.
  • Estates: summary administration is available when the non-exempt estate is $150,000 or less, or when the decedent died more than two years ago.
  • Creditors: claims are barred unless filed by the later of three months after first publication of the notice or 30 days after service on a known creditor.

Florida has no estate tax for deaths after 2004, and the Department of Revenue says personal representatives need not file Forms DR-312 or DR-313 since July 1, 2023.

sections.h2: How does Palm Beach County handle homestead exemptions when a Jupiter house sells?
sections.html:
The exemption ends with your ownership, and the buyer applies separately. The county property appraiser states that all homestead applications must be eligible as of January 1 and submitted by March 1, and that missing the date waives the exemption for that year.

The first $25,000 applies to all taxes, including school district taxes. The additional exemption applies to assessed value above $50,000, excludes school taxes and is adjusted with inflation, and the appraiser lists a 2025 maximum of $25,722. The exemption renews automatically through a receipt card mailed on the last business day of December, but the appraiser says a sale, marriage, divorce, death or change in use needs a call to the office.

A change of ownership resets assessed value to just value the next January 1, which is why a long-held Jupiter homestead can have a very different taxable value for the buyer. The Save Our Homes cap, the lower of 3 percent or the CPI change, then limits the buyer's yearly increases. If you buy again in Florida, ask about portability, which carries part of your savings to a new homestead filed within the state's window.

sections.h2: What transfer costs apply to a Jupiter house sale?
sections.html:
Palm Beach County uses the standard Florida deed tax of 70 cents on each $100 of consideration, and every party to the deed is liable for it regardless of who agrees to pay. Consideration includes mortgages and encumbrances whether or not they are assumed, so a sale subject to a payoff is measured on the full amount.

The clerk collects the tax when recording the deed. Under section 28.24, recording charges are $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each additional page, plus a $1.00 trust fund charge on the first page and $0.50 on others, plus a $4 per page technology charge.

Property tax runs on a calendar the state publishes: assessment on January 1, bills in November, discounts of 4, 3, 2 and 1 percent from November through February, and delinquency on April 1. Your closing agent prorates the year between you and the buyer.

sections.h2: What if a Jupiter house has a lien, foreclosure or tenant?
sections.html:
• Foreclosure: the clerk sells at public sale not less than 20 or more than 35 days after final judgment unless the plaintiff agrees to later, the high bidder posts a 5 percent deposit, and objections are due within 10 days of the certificate of sale.
  • Back taxes: certificate holders may apply for a tax deed after two years have passed since April 1 of the issue year, so clear old balances before they escalate.
  • Tenants: month-to-month tenancies end on at least 30 days' notice, and nonpayment starts with a three-day written notice that excludes weekends and court holidays.

Median gross rent in Jupiter is $2,381 per the Census, so a tenant-occupied house can carry meaningful rental income. Give the buyer the lease before closing.

faqs.q: Is Jupiter a city or a town?
faqs.a: Jupiter is a town. The Census Bureau lists it as Jupiter town, and it sits in Palm Beach County, so the county handles recording, assessment and tax collection.

faqs.q: When must a buyer apply for homestead after buying in Jupiter?
faqs.a: By March 1 of the tax year, having owned and occupied the home on January 1. The Palm Beach County Property Appraiser says missing March 1 waives the exemption for that year.

faqs.q: Does the deed tax rate differ in Palm Beach County?
faqs.a: No. Palm Beach County uses the standard 70 cents per $100 of consideration. Only Miami-Dade County uses a different rate, according to the Department of Revenue.

faqs.q: What happens to my Save Our Homes savings if I sell?
faqs.a: The savings do not stay with the house. A change of ownership resets the assessed value, though you may be able to carry savings to a new Florida homestead through portability by filing with the property appraiser.

faqs.q: Who do I contact about exemption changes?
faqs.a: The Palm Beach County Property Appraiser lists 561.355.2866 and myexemption@pbcpao.gov for changes in ownership or use.
